rule.value: 90 FR 60864 (29 Dec 2025), effective 27 Feb 2026: entries I=1, II=2, III=3, IV=4; below I counts once; several locations use the lowest level

checks.test: run date + hiring lag <= planned registration date
OPT end date >= end of the petition filing window
registration date falls inside the wage year of the data

registration_date.note: USCIS announces the registration window each year; this date is the persona's assumption

latest_offer_date.note: the offer must exist before the employer registers

start_search_by.note: registration date minus the persona's hiring lag

lag_sensitivity.note: the same check with a 30, 60 and 90 day hiring lag

cannot_verify: The SOC code the employer will file. This report assumes 15-1252 (Software Developers); another code moves every threshold.
The actual offered salary. The posted range bounds it only if the employer keeps to its own range.
Whether the employer will register at all, or files using another wage source.
The chance of selection. The entries are relative weights; the real odds depend on the whole year's registration pool.
Which office you would join when a posting lists several cities, or your home address for a remote role.
Whether one posted range is for the listed city or a band for every US location: Pinterest's says 'US based applicants only' and that final salary depends on location.
Anything about the role's quality, the team, or the company's finances.
